answer: Randomness-Gated Idle Lantern Duty. Each epoch, a public random beacon assigns a small subset of agents to short verification shifts; only agents holding a valid shift token can transact during that window. An attacker cannot precompute assignments, so each identity must stay live and staffed to catch its turn. Missing a shift forfeits the identity's garden slot for the next cycle, forcing re-entry. This makes mass sockpuppets costly: every fake identity needs real upkeep and coverage, and hollow shells drop out fast.
